newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Villiger reprises SNB comments from mid-Dec - SNB.
newsitem.headline: Villiger reprises SNB comments from mid-Dec - SNB.

text.p: Swiss Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger's comments that he was "relieved" by the Swiss franc's decline echoed comments the Swiss National Bank (SNB) made in December, an SNB spokesman said.
"I don't think there is any discrepancy between what Mr Villiger said and what the SNB said earlier," the spokesman said.
The spokesman emphasised, however, that the SNB does not comment on day-to-day movements in the currency market.
"We don't have the policy of commenting on shorter-term exchange rate movements in this sense," he added.
Villiger, in an interview with a wire service, said on Monday he was relieved by the Swiss franc's decline.

"I think Mr Villiger's statement was in line with earlier statements made by the National Bank. Let's not forget the bank in mid-December, in presenting its monetary policy, also called the Swiss franc still a firm currency. It was a bit higher...than it is today," the spokesman said.
In its year-end news conference on December 13, SNB board member Bruno Gehrig said that he still viewed the franc as firm, despite its declines.
A finance ministry spokesman earlier pointed out that the SNB and not the ministry was primarily responsible for foreign exchange and monetary policy in Switzerland.
